boardProfile.layout: Block Out level 164 opens on a hard color-sort board dominated by blue, purple, yellow, red, green tiles. The exact starting layout and verified solution are shown in the embedded walkthrough video; match your board to the video before following the move order.
landmarks: The board prominently features blue, purple, and yellow blocks.
Color groups must be separated and stacked to clear the level.
The embedded walkthrough shows the exact starting layout and solution order.

quickTips: Group the blue and purple blocks first — they dominate the opening board, so clearing them early opens the most space.
Keep one column empty as a buffer until your first two merges are done; it is the only safe place to reverse a bad move.
Park mixed or trapped yellow blocks in the shortest column, never the tallest one, so you keep a clean exit lane.
This hard board leaves little margin for error — plan the full exit route before your first move rather than reacting.

steps.title: Match the board
steps.instruction: Confirm the blue/purple layout matches the walkthrough before you move; a different variant means a different solution.
steps.imageAlt: Block Out level board reference for step 1

steps.title: Clear the dominant color
steps.instruction: Merge the blue columns first to free the largest area of the board and reduce the pieces you must track.
steps.imageAlt: Block Out level board reference for step 2

steps.title: Open a buffer lane
steps.instruction: Shift purple blocks aside into one short column so mixed stacks stay separable and the exit lane stays open.
steps.imageAlt: Block Out level board reference for step 3

steps.title: Work top-down
steps.instruction: Clear from the top so nothing locks early; keep the buffer column available until the board is nearly empty.
steps.imageAlt: Block Out level board reference for step 4

steps.title: Route the exit
steps.instruction: Send the last blocks out through the same lane shown in the video, in the order the walkthrough demonstrates.
steps.imageAlt: Block Out level board reference for step 5

failurePoints: Merging the tallest column first burns your only buffer lane and traps the lower blocks behind it.
Chasing a full blue stack before separating mixed colors leaves blocks you can no longer reach.
Starting the timer before the board is matched wastes 8–12 seconds of recovery on a hard board.
Letting purple blocks sit behind others forces a restart you could have avoided with one early shift.
